summary: Task Recaller — records what you were working on and offers it back after a break.
overview: Picks up the thread after you have been away. It records what you had selected and which scripts you opened as you work, and when you come back after a real gap it opens itself with that timeline and a one-click jump back to each item. Runs on its own with nothing to wire up.

features.name: Note field
features.what: a message to your future self, for the intent no tool can infer.

features.name: Timeline
features.what: selections, opened scripts and notes, newest first, each with a button that jumps you back to it.

features.name: Auto-open
features.what: shows itself on the first launch after a gap longer than your away-time setting.

useCases: Coming back on Monday to a task you were mid-way through on Friday.
Leaving yourself a note about what you were about to try, before closing Unity.
Jumping straight back to the prefab or script you were last working in, without hunting for it.
whereToFind: Toolkit ▸ Task Recaller — or it opens itself after a gap

walkthrough.name: Leave a note for next time
walkthrough.what: Free text saved as a timeline entry. Save Note is disabled until you type something.

walkthrough.name: Away-time gap (minutes)
walkthrough.what: How long since your last recorded action before this counts as a new session and the window auto-opens. Defaults to 20.

walkthrough.name: Clear History
walkthrough.what: Deletes the recorded selections and opened scripts. Notes are entries too, so they go as well — it asks first.

walkthrough.name: Select / Open Scene
walkthrough.what: On a timeline row: jumps to the object. If it lived in a different scene, it offers to open that scene first.

gotchas.title: It cannot see inside your code editor
gotchas.body: Unity has no API into VS Code or Rider, so it records only that you double-clicked a script open — not your tabs, cursor position or unsaved edits. The note field is the intended answer to that gap, and it is deliberately not faked.

gotchas.title: The gap is measured per Editor process, not per recompile
gotchas.body: It uses SessionState, which survives a script recompile but resets on a real relaunch. That is what stops the window popping up after every recompile — but it also means the gap only gets checked when Unity actually starts.

gotchas.title: History is per-user and not in version control
gotchas.body: It persists to UserSettings/, the folder Unity reserves for per-user editor state. It will not follow you to another machine and will not appear in a teammate's project.
